El Farruco (1936-1997), autodidacta, fue el patriarca del baile gitano de hombre (Bodas de gloria). El Güito, el más ortodoxo, ganó en 1959 el premio Sarah Bernhardt de París frente a Nureyev. Mario Maya renovó la escena con Camelamos naquerar (1976), con Concha Vargas. Matilde Coral, heredera de Pastora Imperio, maestra de Milagros Menjíbar y María Pagés; Manuela Vargas, «la dama del flamenco»; Tía Juana la del Pipa, que no fue profesional hasta los cuarenta; la Chunga, que bailaba descalza; y Manuela Carrasco, la más importante de su generación, completan el retrato, con las escuelas de Granada (Manolete, Mariquilla) y Córdoba (Concha Calero).

scenes.name: El piano flamenco
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Lorca tocó el piano para la Argentinita y Caracol lo usó en lugar de la guitarra, pero el piano flamenco tiene sus propios nombres. Arturo Pavón (1930), de la familia de los Pavón y de Caracol, formado en el conservatorio, hizo dúo con Luisa Ortega en el tablao Los Canasteros; Pepe Romero (1936-1997) fue el pianista ortodoxo e investigador; Felipe Campuzano, compositor de Andalucía espiritual. Chano Domínguez (1960) viene del jazz y lo une al flamenco; Dorantes (1969), de los Peña de Lebrija, estudió en el conservatorio y Yehudi Menuhin lo llevó a Mont de Marsan; Diego Gallego, de la escuela de Campuzano, ha tocado con Rancapino y Maíta Vende Cá.

scenes.name: El arte jondo: duende y universalidad
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: La tesis de partida: el flamenco, tal como hoy se conoce, tiene poco más de un siglo, pero ha pasado de un desahogo de la Andalucía oprimida, transmitido de generación en generación y disfrutado por unos pocos en reuniones, a un arte mayor aplaudido en los teatros de todo el mundo. La bailaora Cristina Hoyos, en el prólogo, defiende que siga evolucionando con fusiones y mestizajes siempre que no pierda su raíz. Arbelos reúne elogios de voces muy distintas: Manuel de Falla («no hay música más rica, ni más viva en toda Europa»), Stravinski en 1921 («un arte de composición»), Miles Davis en 1950 («es como nuestro blues»), Chick Corea, Unamuno, Pemán, Rubén Darío, Lorca, Juan Ramón Jiménez o Jean Cocteau. Su intemporalidad y universalidad lo ponen a la altura de los clásicos, aunque su cuna sea popular y anónimos sus primeros cultores. Y lo que conmueve al público sin conocimientos previos es el duende: la corriente indefinible que une al intérprete con quien lo escucha. El libro quiere ser una guía sencilla y didáctica para entender lo que se oye en un recital.

scenes.name: Las dinastías de Jerez
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: La ciudad de las bulerías y de las grandes familias gitanas. El Gloria (1893-1954) cantaba saetas y bulerías y creó sus villancicos. Agujeta el Viejo transmitió los cantes de Manuel Torre, y su hijo el Agujetas (1939) tiene la voz rota de los «sonidos negros» de Lorca. Terremoto (1934-1981) fue indispensable en los festivales de los sesenta por siguiriyas y bulerías; el Sordera (1927-2001) brilló en los tablaos de Madrid y dejó una dinastía; el Chocolate (1931), voz de la escuela de Torre, ganó el Giraldillo de la Bienal de 1986 y un Grammy Latino en 2002. Tío Juane cantaba martinetes forjando una herradura y la Paquera (1934) tenía una voz de enorme potencia. José Mercé (1955), de la dinastía de Paco la Luz y cantaor de la compañía de Gades, es a comienzos del siglo XXI el cantaor de más éxito, por unir la raíz jonda con la música de su tiempo. Siguen el Capullo, maestro del compás, Diego Carrasco, cuyo ritmo buscan Camarón o Morente, y la Macanita, la gran cantaora joven de Jerez.

scenes.name: Las bamberas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: El cante que acompañaba el vaivén del columpio, la bamba, en las fiestas campesinas al acabar la cosecha o en las fiestas patronales, con ritmo de soleá lenta. Como todos los cantes folclóricos andaluces que se aflamencaron entre finales del XIX y la primera mitad del XX, su jondura depende del intérprete: unas sevillanas de Camarón son flamencas; las de un coro rociero, canción folclórica. Su creadora indiscutible fue la Niña de los Peines, y Camarón cantó por bamberas «La leyenda del tiempo» de Lorca.

scenes.name: La rumba
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: El cante de ida y vuelta más estudiado, tan parecido al tango que confunde a los investigadores. Según Papa Wemba su melodía es centroafricana, de Zaire: viajó con la trata de esclavos a Cuba y de allí a España. La aportación más flamenca fue la de Pepe de la Matrona, que vivió en Cuba a mediados de la década de 1910 (Recuerdos de La Habana, 1914). La rumba catalana tiene su estilo propio, con el Pescaílla, marido de Lola Flores, y Peret, y su toque rapidísimo «del ventilador». Poco apreciada por los flamencos, ha crecido con la salsa entre el público joven; Paco de Lucía tuvo su primer gran éxito con la rumba «Entre dos aguas» y la «Macarena» de Los del Río batió todos los récords. Su baile es sensual y provocador.

scenes.name: La escuela gaditana
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Los cantaores de Cádiz, herederos del Mellizo, dueños de las cantiñas, los tanguillos y las alegrías. Aurelio Sellés (1887-1974) fue uno de sus puntales y dominó cantiñas, siguiriyas, soleares y malagueñas. Pericón de Cádiz (1901-1980) contó su vida en Las mil y una historias de Pericón. La Perla de Cádiz (1925-1975) recreó los estilos de su tierra. Chano Lobato (1927) es el «dueño del compás»: acompañó a Antonio, Matilde Coral y Manuela Vargas y desde los ochenta canta como solista. Les siguen Rancapino, continuador de Aurelio; Chaquetón, de la saga de los Chaqueta y en la línea del Mellizo; Mariana Cornejo, popular por un anuncio cantado por tanguillos; y Juanito Villar, salido de las comparsas de carnaval, que grabó con Paco Cepero.

scenes.name: Villancicos y zambombas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes navideños sobre el nacimiento del «Niño Manuel», de remoto origen profano (hay quien los deriva del zéjel árabe), que el legendario Niño Gloria de Jerez adaptó al compás de bulerías, tangos y tanguillos; sus villancicos los conocen todos los artistas. José Mercé los recreó con gran jondura en la serie Así canta nuestra tierra por Navidad (doce volúmenes), con el tocaor Parrilla de Jerez y el aula de folclore de la Cátedra de Flamencología. En Jerez se celebran por Navidad las zambombas: reuniones familiares en patios de vecinos o bodegas donde se canta en corro por bulerías y tangos, se baila en el centro y se comen pestiños.

scenes.name: Las bulerías
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: El cante festero por excelencia, con el compás de la soleá mucho más acelerado; nacido a comienzos del siglo XX (Mairena atribuye al Loco Mateo, en el XIX, el remate acelerado de las soleares). Tiene dos centros: Cádiz, más larga y suave, y Jerez, más corta y bulliciosa, «la ciudad de los gitanos» de Lorca, donde hasta las piedras cantan por bulerías y el soniquete se lleva en la sangre. El nombre se discute: burla, bolero o bulla. Su métrica lo admite todo, coplas de soleá, seguidillas o canciones (en Utrera, letras de canciones ajenas): un buen cantaor podría cantar por bulerías la guía telefónica. Cierra cualquier festival en el fin de fiesta, y quien la domina en el cante, el baile o el toque domina todo el flamenco.

scenes.name: Los cantes de ida y vuelta: colombiana, guajira, vidalita, milonga
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes folclóricos hispanoamericanos (rumba, milonga, colombiana, guajira, vidalita) aflamencados por la manera de cantarlos en Andalucía; fáciles de cantar, no se consideran cante jondo. Llegaron en la última década del XIX y se difundieron desde los años treinta: son la última gran incorporación al flamenco. La idea de que eran cantes andaluces que fueron a América y volvieron es pura mitopoética. Sabicas contaba que él y Vicente Escudero, con muchos contratos en América y el repertorio flamenco agotado, empezaron a tocar esas canciones «con este aire nuestro». La colombiana no viene de América: la creó Pepe Marchena en los treinta, con enorme éxito; Carmen Amaya fue la primera en cantarla y bailarla, Sabicas la tocaba sin nombrarla por vergüenza y Juanito Valderrama popularizó la suya en los cincuenta. La guajira, de Cuba, fue la primera en llegar y la que mejor se adaptó (en Cádiz se cantaban «guajiras festeras» por bulerías); sus coplas son décimas. La vidalita, del norte argentino y triste, la recuperaron en los noventa jóvenes como Mayte Martín; la milonga pampeana la trajo Pepa Oro en compás de tangos, Chacón la remataba por tanguillos y Pepe de la Matrona la grabó. Hay dos discos fundamentales: Cantes de ida y vuelta (Junta de Andalucía, 1985, con Menese, José Mercé y Luis de Córdoba) y Dos mundos cantan (Expo 92, con Valderrama, Rocío Jurado y Chano Lobato).

scenes.name: Las saetas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cante dolido que solo se canta en Semana Santa, al paso de las imágenes, a palo seco o con cornetas y tambores, por martinetes, siguiriyas (las más comunes), soleares, cañas o polos, con coplas de exaltación religiosa que exigen gran potencia de voz. Nace a finales del XIX en Cádiz: Enrique el Mellizo y sus hijos detenían al Nazareno desde los cuatro balcones de su casa con sus saetas. A él se atribuye la saeta por siguiriyas, que desarrolló Manuel Centeno en el siglo XX. Manuel Torre, el Niño Gloria, la Niña de los Peines, Manolo Caracol y Antonio Mairena eran esperados en Semana Santa para cantarlas sin amplificación desde un balcón a la altura de las imágenes; Manuel Mairena grabó un vía crucis entero. Un equipo francés grabó en directo a los saeteros de Jerez, Arcos y Lebrija en la Semana Santa de 1993 para la colección Flamenco vivo.

scenes.name: Demófilo y los Machado
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Antonio Machado y Álvarez, Demófilo, fue el primer autor español que dedicó un libro entero al flamenco: la Colección de cantes flamencos recogidos y anotados (1881), piedra angular de la flamencología moderna; escribió también sobre las saetas y dirigió la revista El Folclore Andaluz (1882-1883). Sus hijos, los poetas Antonio y Manuel Machado (autor de Cante hondo), heredaron la afición, y sus coplas se cantan a menudo sin que los cantaores sepan que son versos cultos. Calixto Sánchez dedicó a Antonio Machado un disco en 2001, y José Menese hizo suyas las letras de Francisco Moreno Galván.

scenes.name: La farruca y el garrotín
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes aflamencados de fuera de Andalucía. La farruca, gallega, llegó a Cádiz con los comerciantes gallegos del XIX y es más baile que cante; la popularizó Manuel Torre a principios del XX y hoy casi solo la canta Pepe Menese, con una letra de Moreno Galván que se hizo himno en la Transición. Su baile, viril, lo creó Faíco; Carmen Amaya lo bailó vestida de hombre, Falla lo incluyó en El sombrero de tres picos y la versión de Antonio Gades en la película de Los Tarantos, la última de Carmen Amaya, se enseña hoy en las academias. El garrotín viene del folclore asturiano y lo hicieron suyo los gitanos de Lleida; lo difundieron Carmen Amaya y la Niña de los Peines, que lo cantaba con aire de tangos, Faíco hizo sus coreografías y Blas Vega recogió una copla antigua cantada por el Chaparro en la Magna antología del cante flamenco.

scenes.name: Los fandangos de Huelva
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Huelva reclama la cuna del fandango andaluz y es la provincia con más estilos: las antologías recogen más de treinta y cinco, locales (Encinasola, el Alosno, Cabezas Rubias, Calañas, el Andévalo, Valverde del Camino) y personales, creados por profesionales como Paco Isidro, Pepe Rebollo, el Comía, Antonio Rengel, Pérez de Guzmán y Paco Toronjo; de fuera dejaron su sello el Gloria, Macandé, el Carbonerillo y Manolo Caracol. Paco Toronjo, fijo en los festivales desde finales de los sesenta y en las bienales de Sevilla, les dio una jondura difícil de imitar. El baile, de pareja y galanteo, se ve ya poco.

scenes.name: Los cantes de Levante o de las minas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Nacidos del trabajo en las minas del siglo XIX en las sierras de Cartagena y La Unión y en Linares, La Carolina y Andújar: cantes de dolor profundo sobre la mina, sus accidentes y los compañeros muertos, hechos con fandangos regionales, murcianas, malagueñas y el cante de madrugá de los mineros. La taranta, el más significativo, tiene dos estilos, el de Linares (Gabriel Moreno, Carmen Linares) y el de La Unión (Encarnación Fernández, Pepe Cros), y Camarón le puso dulzura; el taranto, almeriense, tiene compás porque nació para el baile de Carmen Amaya en los cuarenta, con el Ciego de la Playa y Pedro el Morato. La cartagenera, de temas más urbanos, la fijó Antonio Chacón a finales del XIX y la cantaron Cayetano Muriel, Manuel Centeno, Manuel Torre y la Niña de los Peines. La minera se atribuye a Rojo el Alpargatero, Antonio Grau Mora, que hacia 1885 abrió en La Unión una posada que acabó en café cantante y oía cantar a los mineros de madrugada: es el gran creador de los cantes mineros. Las granaínas, de Frasquito Yerbabuena y sobre todo Chacón, son un cante casi barroco hoy cargado de vibratos operísticos. Sin minas, los concursos de Linares y La Unión mantienen vivos estos cantes.

scenes.name: Las cantiñas: alegrías, caracoles, mirabrás y romeras
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes alegres de la bahía de Cádiz, en compás de soleá y muy ligados al baile, que arranca majestuoso y va ganando fuerza hasta desplantes electrizantes. Nacen probablemente de la jotilla gaditana, hermanada con la jota aragonesa por la resistencia común contra Napoleón, de ahí las letras sobre la guerra y el mar; la leyenda atribuye su creación a Enrique el Mellizo, que oyó a una muchacha cantar jotas con un ciego. Tomaron identidad en la segunda mitad del XIX. Hay cantiñas del Pinini de Utrera y Lebrija y de Córdoba; la rosa ya no se canta. Las alegrías, al principio baile de mujer sola, se hicieron más lentas a comienzos del XX y empiezan con el «tirititrán» que, según Chano Lobato, inventó Pericón de Cádiz al olvidar la letra; las cantaron el Mellizo, Ignacio Ezpeleta, Aurelio Sellés, Manolo Vargas y Pericón. Los caracoles, de Tío José el Granaíno (picador del Chiclanero), los recreó Chacón y triunfaron en Madrid («la gran calle de Alcalá»). El mirabrás son alegrías largas (José Menese, con letras de Moreno Galván), y las romeras se atribuyen al Granaíno o a una cantaora llamada la Romera. Hoy el gran intérprete es Chano Lobato.

scenes.name: Los tangos, tientos y marianas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Con bulerías y cantiñas, el gran cante festero: letras de vida, amor y muerte con cierta ligereza, ritmo vivo y pegadizo fácil de seguir con palmas, y un baile sensual. Cádiz y Sevilla se disputan su paternidad, pero los hay en toda Andalucía y en Extremadura; Triana tiene el estilo del Titi y Jerez su propio sello. Su origen musical se discute: Mairena los tenía por cante básico gitano; los estudios recientes los llevan a Cuba y las habaneras llegadas a Sevilla y Cádiz en la segunda mitad del XIX; los granadinos defienden una raíz morisca (el disco Granada canta por tangos recoge trece estilos, entre ellos los de la morería). Manuel Ríos Ruiz concluye que no se sabe con certeza. La Niña de los Peines se hizo inmortal con su copla «Péinate tú con mis peines». Del tango nacen los tientos, más pausados y solemnes, que cantaron primero el Mellizo y el Marrurro y se popularizaron a comienzos del XX, y la mariana, que difundió Bernardo el de los Lobitos y hoy casi solo canta Pepe Menese con letras de Moreno Galván.

scenes.name: Las soleares
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: La madre del cante y uno de sus pilares, independiente de cualquier otro ritmo; los cantaores la consideran «el toro bravo del arte jondo». Coplas solemnes y sentenciosas de tres o cuatro octosílabos, unidas por la guitarra, que suelen rematarse por bulerías; muy apropiadas para el baile de mujer. Se desarrolló al sur del Guadalquivir desde los jaleos festivos: la primera mención es de la Andonda en Triana hacia 1840, una cantaora temible contemporánea del Fillo, y tomó su forma actual entre 1875 y 1915. Las mujeres fueron clave en su creación y transmisión (la Andonda, Mercedes la Serneta, Fernanda de Utrera, Carmen Linares). Hay soleares de Triana (la Andonda, Silverio, Fernando el de Triana, la Niña de los Peines, Tomás Pavón, Mairena), de Alcalá, más solemnes (Joaquín el de la Paula, Juan Talega), de Utrera (la Serneta, el Pinini, María Peña, Fernanda), de Cádiz y el Puerto, más jondas (Enrique Butrón, el Mellizo, Paquirri el Guanté), de Jerez, breves y llenas de melismas (Curro Frijones, José Illanda, Juan Mojama, Tío José de Paula, Manuel Torre) y de Córdoba, más pausadas.

scenes.name: Las siguiriyas, livianas y serranas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Una de las expresiones más dramáticas y de los palos más importantes: sin siguiriyas y soleares el flamenco no sería lo que es. Un quejío entero de lamentos que no admite medias tintas («con las siguiriyas no se puede vender la burra»), con coplas trágicas de cuatro versos (6, 6, 10 y 6 sílabas), muchas sobre la muerte de los seres queridos, y falsetas lentas que suenan a campanas a muerto. Lorca la describió como un grito terrible que divide el paisaje en dos; Tía Anica la Piriñaca decía que cuando la cantaba a gusto la boca le sabía a sangre. La cantaban ya el Planeta (la de la Luna, la más antigua conocida) y el Fillo; luego Manuel Torre, Silverio, Paco la Luz, Cagancho, el Nitri, Curro Dulce, el Loco Mateo, el Mellizo, Terremoto de Jerez (que cantó toda la noche por siguiriyas con su madre muerta en brazos) y Juan Talega; hoy el Chocolate y José Menese. Antonio Mairena grabó unas cuarenta y cinco formas: es el siguiriyero más importante. Sus escuelas son Jerez y los Puertos, Cádiz y Triana. En el baile la difundió Vicente Escudero y Pilar López le añadió los palillos. La liviana, cante de campo, caminos y bandoleros, prepara la voz para la serrana, a la que Silverio dio brillo y con la que se remata por siguiriyas.

scenes.name: La caña, el polo y la petenera
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Tres cantes de la familia de la soleá. La caña, con ayes más arrastrados, se sitúa en la serranía de Ronda (un viajero inglés la oyó allí en 1830) o en la voz árabe gaunia, «canción»; la cantaron el Fillo, Tío José el Granaíno, Antonio Chacón, Pepe de la Matrona y Rafael Romero el Gallina, y hoy se usa más para el baile solemne. El polo se cantaba tras la caña, con la misma métrica; el de Tobalo, su supuesto creador, aparece ya en Estébanez Calderón y hoy se usa en la soleá apolá; Enrique Morente grabó el de Chacón. La petenera, melancólica y de origen incierto, se atribuye a una mujer de Paterna de la Ribera, «la perdición de los hombres», o a los sefardíes de los Balcanes; los gitanos la evitaron porque traía mala suerte. La cantaron la Niña de los Peines, Naranjito de Triana, Rafael Romero, Fosforito y hoy Pepe Menese.

scenes.name: Los cantes de Málaga: malagueñas, rondeñas, jaberas y verdiales
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Después de Sevilla y Cádiz, Málaga es la provincia con más variedad de cantes. La malagueña, cante libre, sin medida y sin baile, de rico toque, ha influido en las granaínas y en todos los cantes minero-levantinos. Nació en Álora (las malagueñas perotas) a partir de los fandangos abandolaos, acompañados de bandola; tras los anónimos y los de Cipriano Pitana, Francisco Jiménez y Joaquín Tabaco, Juan Breva le dio identidad propia, y Lorca escribió de su trino. Su esplendor es la segunda mitad del XIX, con el Canario, la Trini, Baldomero Pacheco y Fosforito el Viejo; también firmaron malagueñas el Mellizo, único gitano creador de una (inspirada en el prefacio de la misa), y Chacón. Diego Clavel recogió treinta y una en los noventa. La rondeña, de principios del XIX y de la tierra del Tobalo, es la pieza con que muchos guitarristas abren sus conciertos; la jabera, ruda y difícil, debe su nombre a una vendedora de habas y está casi perdida; los verdiales, de probable raíz morisca, apenas han cambiado y conservan la panda con violín, panderos, chinchines y cañas para la fiesta de san Juan.

scenes.name: Los tanguillos de Cádiz
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Vinculados al carnaval de Cádiz, son el soporte de chirigotas, coros y murgas; cantados en grupo pierden su naturaleza flamenca, que es individual, aunque como baile la conservan. Hay constancia de los «tangos graciosos» del barrio de La Viña en 1779, en la tonadilla La anónima de Tomás Abril, y el tango americano o de negros terminó de formarlos. Letras jocosas y satíricas: «el chiste ingenuo y feliz enfrente de la tragedia jonda del quejío» (Emilio Jiménez Díaz). Aurelio y Pericón de Cádiz, Manuel Vargas y la Perla los grabaron en la primera mitad del siglo XX, y hasta Mairena dejó dos. Chano Lobato, su mayor cultor, los elevó a cante noble y recrea la venta de los cuadros que popularizó Pericón.

scenes.name: Las tonás: martinetes, carceleras y deblas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes sin acompañamiento, prueba de su antigüedad, en cuartetas octosílabas de intensa carga dramática y origen gitano indiscutible: son crónicas de la miseria, la cárcel y la persecución. Demófilo ya las daba en 1881 por «cantes viejos casi caídos en desuso»; en el siglo XIX hubo entre veintisiete y treinta y cuatro, cada una con el nombre de su creador. La más antigua es la de Tío Luis el de la Juliana, aguador y primer cantaor del que hay noticia (segunda mitad del siglo XVIII), conservada por Antonio Chacón y recreada por Pepe de la Matrona; se le atribuye también la toná de los pajaritos, que recuerda la tonada sefardí de los bilbilicos. Los martinetes toman el nombre del martillo de la fragua, aunque es difícil cantar mientras se forja: Tío Juane de Jerez montaba una fragua en escena en los setenta y ochenta, y Antonio el Bailarín creó su baile con martillo y yunque; la familia fragüera más antigua es la de los Cantorales de Cádiz, que Silverio visitaba. Las carceleras cantan la prisión y servían para pasar mensajes en romaní desde las rejas. La debla, único palo con nombre romaní («diosa»), es religiosa, casi perdida y muy difícil; llegó a hoy por Tomás Pavón en los cuarenta y la recuperó Antonio Mairena.

scenes.name: Las sevillanas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Nacen de las seguidillas castellanas, que en Sevilla se hicieron más vivas y fáciles de repetir: cuatro coplas para bailar en pareja un galanteo, con temas andaluces, amorosos o rocieros (corraleras, rocieras, bíblicas, de feria, marineras, romeras). Lorca recogió una del siglo XVIII. Su gran auge comercial llegó en los setenta, con millones de discos que daban envidia a los flamencos; las han grabado con jondura Manuel Vallejo, la Niña de los Peines, la Paquera de Jerez, el Turronero, Chiquetete y Camarón.

scenes.name: El fandango
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Muy apreciado por su musicalidad y fácil de interpretar, no es un palo básico pero no es menor: la vieja división entre cantes grandes y chicos está obsoleta, y la jondura la pone el intérprete, no la antigüedad del palo. Canto para bailar de origen muy antiguo e incierto (Corominas lo deriva del portugués fado; hay quien le ve un lejano origen árabe), aparece por escrito en un entremés de 1705 y lo describe el deán Manuel Martí en 1712; en el siglo XIX fue el cante y baile nacional español, y a finales de siglo se aflamencó en Andalucía y dejó de bailarse. De él salen las granaínas, las malagueñas y los cantes de Levante, y hay fandangos propios en Lucena, Cabra, Puente Genil, Jaén, Granada o Almería. Su apogeo en la ópera flamenca lo desprestigió tanto que a cantaores como Pepe Menese les parece un insulto que se lo pidan; desde los años ochenta se revaloriza.

facts.title: Bitter Split from Tony DeFries (April 1975)
facts.body: Following Bowie's decision to split from Tony DeFries, a 48-hour marathon negotiation took place in April 1975 to finalize his departure. The terms of the split were so harsh that it's said Bowie broke down and cried at the conference table, remaining in shock for a week. The agreement stipulated that Bowie could leave only if Main Man took half of his earnings from albums dating back to *Hunky Dory* in 1971 through an upcoming live album, and DeFries was guaranteed 16% of Bowie's gross earnings for the next seven years, through to 1982.
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Mighty Managers of Rock
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Mainstream Crossover Success (1975)
facts.body: By 1975, with the "Young Americans" album, Bowie had become a global superstar whose music transcended genre boundaries. His songs were played on both Top 40 and rock radio stations, and he was considered cool in punk clubs. Tracks like "Fame" or "Young Americans" were even mixed in among dance music in disco clubs. "He was one of the biggest stars in the world."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Remembering David Bowie: Part 1
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: British Punk Favorite - 1975
facts.body: By 1975, Bowie had become a favorite among British punks, who admired not only his music but also his non-status quo fashion sense and his defiant attitude. His influence was so strong that it was difficult to find a punk enthusiast in London who wasn't also a Bowie fan. "By 1975, he'd become a favorite among British punks."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Why Bowie Still Matters - Part 2
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Severe Addiction and Health Crisis - 1975-1976
facts.body: During the period from late 1975 to late 1976, Bowie was heavily drinking and consuming tremendous amounts of cocaine, while subsisting on little more than milk and peppers. His weight plummeted to less than 90 pounds, indicating a severe health crisis, and he was described as "cracking up." "Bowie was drinking very heavily and using tremendous amounts of cocaine while eating a little more than milk and peppers."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Why Bowie Still Matters - Part 2
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Early Label Rejection & Sire Signing (1975)
facts.body: The Ramones were signed by Seymour Stein to Sire Records in 1975 after he discovered them in a Manhattan bar. Other labels refused to sign them because they were considered "too weird," played "too fast," were "too amateurish," and "too funny looking." Mainstream rock radio also rejected them, seeing them as a joke. "back then, nobody wanted to touch the Ramones. They were just too weird. They played too fast. They were too amateurish. And they were too funny looking for all the other labels."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 1
facts.name: The Ramones

facts.title: Admiration and Friendship in New York (1975)
facts.body: Upon moving to New York in 1975, Poison Ivy and Lux Interior became frequent visitors to CBGB, where they met the Ramones. They declared themselves fans of the Ramones and developed a good friendship with them. "Allí conocieron a los Ramones, de los que se declararon fans y hicieron buenas migas."
facts.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps
facts.name: The Ramones

facts.title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show Costumes (1975)
facts.body: The costumes designed by Sue Blaine for *The Rocky Horror Picture Show* in 1975, featuring wild multicolored hair, crazy makeup, and fishnet stockings, were noted for their punk rock aesthetic, emerging around the time punk was just beginning. Blaine claimed to have improvised the designs with a budget of only $1,600, possibly influencing early punk fashion. "Wild multicolored hair, crazy makeup, fishnet stockings. Did the movie influence the fashion of punk rock? Maybe."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Key Alt-Rock Movie Soundtracks
facts.name: Punk Rock

facts.title: Term Definition by "Punk" Magazine (1975)
facts.body: The fanzine "Punk," launched at the end of 1975, was crucial in defining the term. It covered artists like Lou Reed, The Ramones, Iggy Pop, The Stooges, The New York Dolls, and 60s garage bands. Its name, inspired by The Dictators' 1975 album "Go Girl Crazy," solidified "punk" as the descriptor for the new, stripped-down rock and roll sound and the artists associated with the CBGB scene. "And so, the authors of this fanzine decided to call their publication, Punk. And as the CBGB scene grew bigger, circulation increased, and soon anyone who was featured in the fanzine was known as a punk artist."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 3
facts.name: Punk Rock

facts.title: Global Germination (1975)
facts.body: By 1975, punk rock had started "germinating" in New York, with significant contributions from the Cleveland music scene, indicating its early spread and development beyond a single geographical origin. "By 1975, punk rock had started germinating in New York, thanks to help from Cleveland."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 3
facts.name: Punk Rock

facts.title: First Gig (1975)
facts.body: The Sex Pistols' first public performance took place on November 6th, 1975. The band had been together for just over a year before releasing their debut single, "Anarchy in the UK." "The first gig had been on November 6th of 1975."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 10
facts.name: The Sex Pistols

facts.title: Formation and Johnny Rotten's Audition (1975)
facts.body: In 1975, Malcolm McLaren, the former manager of The New York Dolls and co-proprietor of the "Sex" clothing shop at 430 King's Road in London's Chelsea area, sought to form a band as a living advertisement for his store. He liked the name "Pistols" for its dangerous connotation, thus "Sex Pistols." Malcolm was looking for a singer and was introduced to 19-year-old Johnny Lydon (later Johnny Rotten), who had green teeth and was spotted by Bernie Rhodes wearing a homemade "I hate Pink Floyd" t-shirt held together with safety pins. Despite Lydon's inability to sing, Malcolm had him audition by miming and "singing" Alice Cooper's "I'm 18" to a jukebox in the shop, which landed him the role. "So Malcolm got young John to audition, not caring if Johnny could actually sing a note, which he couldn't."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 8
facts.name: The Sex Pistols

facts.title: Formation and Vision (1975)
facts.body: Malcolm McLaren conceived the Sex Pistols as a living, breathing advertisement for his Kings Road shop, which by then was renamed Sex. The band was also intended to be an outlet for McLaren's semi-seditious political beliefs, designed to shock and shake up the stuffy British establishment. McLaren assembled the group using "snotty kids" who frequented his store, naming them "Sex" after his shop and "Pistols" because it sounded dangerous.
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Mighty Managers of Rock
facts.name: The Sex Pistols

facts.title: First Gig (November 1975)
facts.body: The Sex Pistols played their first gig in November 1975, the same month Patti Smith released her influential debut album "Horses." They were contemporaries of The Slits and a foundational band of the punk movement. "That was the same month the sex pistols played their first gig"
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Riot Grrrls - A Primer
facts.name: The Sex Pistols

facts.title: First Live Performance (November 6, 1975)
facts.body: The band's first live gig took place in London at an art school called St. Martin's. It was held in a small upstairs room with only a dozen people in attendance, who were primarily there to see the headliners, Bizzouca Joe, featuring Adam Ant. The Sex Pistols' performance was cut short after only two songs when the school's social programmer pulled the plug. Despite the brevity and lack of immediate success, this event marked a significant turning point in music history. "And despite the fact that their first live gig wasn't much of a hit, music was never to be quite the same."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 1000th Episode of the Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Sex Pistols

facts.title: First Live Gig (November 6, 1975)
facts.body: The Sex Pistols' first live performance occurred on November 6, 1975, at St. Martin's art school in London. They played as an unexpected opening act for Vasuka Jo (featuring Adam Ant), but their set was cut short by the school's social programmer after just "p**tongs" because the audience had "heard enough." Despite this, it was considered a pivotal moment that changed music. "The name of that band was the sex pistols. And despite the fact that their first live gig wasn't much of a hit, music was never to be quite the same."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 500th Show!
facts.name: The Sex Pistols

facts.title: Formation Anecdote (1975)
facts.body: The formation of the Sex Pistols and Johnny Rotten's recruitment in 1975 is marked by a notable anecdote involving Malcolm McLaren's clothing shop. Rotten's "I Hate Pink Floyd" t-shirt served as an instant identifier of his anti-establishment attitude, leading to his consideration as the band's frontman. "He was immediately considered for the job of lead singer of the sex pistols, based on the fact that he was wearing an eye-hate pink Floyd t-shirt."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 15
facts.name: The Sex Pistols

facts.title: Impact on UK Music Scene (1975)
facts.body: The Sex Pistols were identified as one of three bands, alongside The Clash and The Saints, that "changed the music forever in the UK," following the media frenzy over The Saints' 1976 single. Their emergence in England coincided with the germination of punk rock in New York by 1975. "Because of that media freak out, three bands changed the music forever in the UK, the sex pistols, the clash, and the Saints."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 3
facts.name: The Sex Pistols

facts.title: First Public Performance (1975) - Art School Debut
facts.body: The band's first show was on November 6, 1975, at an art school. Despite the venue, the student organizer was so repulsed by the performance that he cut the electricity to the stage after just 10 minutes. "Their first show was on November the 6th, 1975."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 4
facts.name: The Sex Pistols

facts.title: Perceived Danger (1975-1976)
facts.body: When they emerged in 1975-1976, The Sex Pistols were considered seriously dangerous. They embodied the rage of Britain's underemployed young working class, expressing disdain for the monarchy and hatred for the social order and class system. Their snotty attitude, shocking dress, and aggressive music made them a "clear and present danger" to UK society. "Back then in 75, 76, they were considered to be seriously dangerous to everybody."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Most Dangerous Artists in Rock
facts.name: The Sex Pistols

facts.body: By 1975, record companies started producing 7-inch records specifically labeled "for disco DJs only," as this format was easier for DJs to work with. "Seven inch records that were labeled for disco DJs only were produced because they were easier for DJs to work with."

facts.title: "Four on the Floor" Dominance (1975)
facts.body: In the second half of 1975, "four on the floor" dance music became increasingly prevalent on the radio, with multiple hits in this style charting between late summer and New Year's Eve. "In the second half of 1975, this four on the floor dance music was becoming more and more prevalent on the radio."
facts.episode: Ep. 1 - Disco Doesn't Suck (Encore)

facts.title: Transformative Live Performance (September 11, 1975)
facts.body: Andy McCluskey of OMD saw Kraftwerk perform at the Liverpool Empire on this date, an event he credits with transforming his life and inspiring OMD's musical direction. Paul Humphreys, being 15, was unable to attend due to his mother's rules. "I went to go and see Kraftwerk play at the Liverpool Empire on September the 11th, 1975. And that transformed my life."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Golden Age of Synths as told by OMD
facts.name: Kraftwerk

facts.title: Synthesizer and Rhythm Machine Mastery (1975)
facts.body: By 1975, Kraftwerk was already extensively using synthesizers and rhythm machines to create sounds that contained elements of many future music styles. Their innovative use of these instruments showcased the potential for electronic music to evolve into diverse forms. "you can hear all the elements of all sorts of future music in what craftwork was doing with their synthesizers and rhythm machines as far back as 1975."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 4: Alt-Dance
facts.name: Kraftwerk

facts.title: 1975 Lineup Changes
facts.body: In 1975, when Bob Welch left the band, Lindsey Buckingham was invited to join. Buckingham stipulated that his girlfriend, Stevie Nicks, also be accepted into the band. This led to American folk rock singer-songwriters Buckingham and Nicks joining Mick Fleetwood (drums), John McVie (bass), and Christine McVie (keyboards, singer-songwriter). "in 1975 Lindsey Buckingham insisted that his girlfriend Stevie Nicks be accepted into what remained of Fleetwood Mac at that time when Lindsey Buckingham was invited to fill the void. That was left when Bob Welch left the band so you have a pair of American folk rock singer songwriters Buckingham and Nicks joining the drummer Mick Fleetwood the bassist John McVee and keyboard player and singer songwriter Christine McVee yes John's wife."
facts.episode: Ep. 51 - The Softer Side of 70s Rock
facts.name: Fleetwood Mac

facts.title: Slow Rise to Number One - Fleetwood Mac (1975) Album
facts.body: The 1975 self-titled Fleetwood Mac album achieved an unusual chart record for the longest climb to number one in Billboard album chart history up to that date, taking 58 weeks to reach the top. To this day, it ranks third for the slowest rise, trailing only the *O Brother, Where Art Thou?* soundtrack and a Kid Laroi album. "It was the longest climb to number one in Billboard album chart history to that date."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: Thinking About Tomorrow Edition Part 1
facts.name: Fleetwood Mac

facts.title: Messianic Status in Africa (1975)
facts.body: Following a 1975 visit to Africa, where he was treated with immense reverence "like a combination of Elvis and some other sort of king," James Brown described his role as messianic, asserting, "People look on me as a Messiah in Africa because they see I can bring all black people together." He also recounted being called "the most powerful black man in America" after helping to stop riots in Washington. "People look on me as a Messiah in Africa because they see I can bring all black people together."
facts.episode: Ep. 33 - Zaire '74, Muhammad Ali, and The Rumble in the Jungle
facts.name: James Brown

facts.title: Lou Reed's "Metal Machine Music" Release (1975)
facts.body: RCA released Lou Reed's experimental double album "Metal Machine Music" in the summer of 1975, not out of artistic support, but as a retaliatory move against Reed who was trying to get out of his contract. Reed was contractually obligated to deliver more albums and delivered this avant-garde work of noise and feedback, which RCA, in an "in-your-face" response, put out to the public. "RCA said, screw you and released it as an in-your-face move back at Lou."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Distortion and Feedback
facts.name: RCA Records

facts.title: Contract Dispute with Lou Reed (1975)
facts.body: In 1975, RCA Records was in a contract dispute with Lou Reed, who wished to terminate his agreement. The label insisted he fulfill his contractual obligation of delivering a certain number of albums. "He wanted out of his contract, but RCA was adamant. He had to provide them with the required number of albums as stipulated in his contract."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 3: Industrial
facts.name: RCA Records

facts.title: Cultural Antagonism (1975)
facts.body: In 1975, a t-shirt emblazoned with "I Hate Pink Floyd" worn by Johnny Rotten played a symbolic role in his recruitment for the Sex Pistols. This demonstrated a clear generational and stylistic antagonism, with punk rock emerging in stark opposition to the established progressive rock acts like Pink Floyd. "He was immediately considered for the job of lead singer of the sex pistols, based on the fact that he was wearing an eye-hate pink Floyd t-shirt."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 15
facts.name: The Pink Floyd

facts.title: Stadium-Filling Popularity (1975)
facts.body: In 1975, Pink Floyd was a prominent progressive rock band capable of filling stadiums, illustrating the genre's widespread appeal in the market during that period. "Pin Floyd llena a bastadios."
facts.episode: GENESIS con Peter Gabriel VS. Phil Collins
facts.name: The Pink Floyd

facts.title: Emotional Impact of Sid Baret's 1975 Appearance
facts.body: Sid Baret's shocking appearance in the studio during the recording of "Wish You Were Here" in 1975, where he was completely shaven, pale, and lacked eyebrows and eyelashes, had a profound and lasting impact on the band. Roger Waters was reportedly brought to tears, and the event changed the band's life and history forever. "Roger Waters rompía llorar totalmente desgarrado por el estado en el que estaba Sid Baret. Se quedaron tan impaltados que su vida y la historia de la banda cambiaría para siempre."
facts.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett
facts.name: The Pink Floyd

facts.title: "Pinball Wizard" Film Role (1975)
facts.body: Elton John reportedly agreed to play the Pinball Wizard in the 1975 movie version of *Tommy* and cover the song under the condition that he could keep the enormous boots, which made him appear approximately ten feet tall. In the film, his character's instrument was a pinball machine integrated with a keyboard, and he wore his characteristic sparkly glasses, a sparkly beanie topped with a pinball, and the signature boots, perfectly embodying the 1975 aesthetic. "Elton reportedly agreed to play the pinball wizard and cover the song if he could keep the enormous boots that made him about 10 feet tall."

facts.title: Influential Albums (1975-1979)
facts.body: Between 1975 and 1979, Patti Smith released four very important and extremely influential albums. These works were bold, filled with strong statements and opinions on diverse topics such as religion, racism, feminist principles, and the state of society, profoundly changing the lives of many female punks and future Riot Girls, as well as many guys. "She released four very important and extremely influential albums between 1975 and 1979."

facts.title: Prominent Artist in New York Scene (1975)
facts.body: Patti Smith was identified as one of the leading artists in the emerging New York music scene in 1975, a movement centered around the legendary CBGB club. "En Nueva York estaban emergiendo una escena liderada por bandas como Ramones, Televisión, Patie Smith, Suicide, Blondie or Tolkien Hets."

facts.title: Significant Radio Popularity (1975-1977)
facts.body: Between 1975 and 1977, "over 150 radio stations in the United States had switched to soft rock or what some were calling mellow rock." This substantial shift underscores the genre's growing commercial appeal and the influence of corporate analysis of listener habits in radio programming during the 1970s. "According to a 1977 New York Daily News article over 150 radio stations in the United States had switched to soft rock or what some were calling mellow rock since 1975."

facts.title: Union Rules and Video Innovation (1975)
facts.body: Queen faced a significant hurdle with the British Musicians Union rules, which strictly prohibited lip-syncing on television. This made it impossible for them to perform their complex song "Bohemian Rhapsody" live on TV while maintaining its integrity. To circumvent these rules, they created the innovative "Bohemian Rhapsody" video, which became a landmark in music video history. "Why? Because the rules of the British Musicians Union prohibited lip syncing on TV."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Rise and Fall and Future of the Music Video - Part 1
facts.name: Queen

facts.title: Kraftwerk's Influence (1975)
facts.body: Andy McCluskey's life was transformed after seeing Kraftwerk perform at the Liverpool Empire on September 11, 1975. This experience inspired the band to pursue alternative electronic music, though Paul Humphreys, being 15, missed the concert due to his mother's age restrictions. "No, we got fascinated by doing alternative music inspired by Kraftwerk and other German rights."

facts.title: Seven-Week CBGB Residency with Patti Smith (Spring 1975)

"For seven weeks in the spring of 1975 television and the Paddy Smith group alternated between being the opening act and the closing act two sets of night, four nights a week."

facts.title: First Domestic Signing (The Ramones - 1975)
facts.body: In 1975, Seymour Stein discovered the Ramones in a Manhattan bar and signed them, making them one of Sire's first domestic signings. This was significant as other labels had rejected the Ramones for being too unconventional. "But then in 1975, Seymour decided to check out a bar in one of the scusiest parts of Manhattan and this is where he found the Ramones and they became one of Sire's first domestic signings."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Peter Gabriel Left 1975; Phil Collins Replaced Him After 40 Auditions; Ray Wilson Later Filled In
facts.body: Peter Gabriel was Genesis's founding singer from 1967 until his departure in 1975, which nearly ended the band. After approximately 40 auditions, they chose their own drummer Phil Collins, whose tenure extended the band's commercial reach considerably. In 1996–2000, when Collins was occupied with his solo career, a singer named Ray Wilson fronted the band before Collins returned. "You know, that worked out okay, didn't it?"
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: 18 Bands Who Changed Lead Singers
facts.name: Genesis

facts.title: Resistance to Commercialism and Industry Pressures (1975)
facts.body: At 26 years old in 1975, Billy Joel vocalized a strong aversion to being "commercial" and "play[ing] the game" of the music industry. He explicitly refused to host shows like *Midnight Special* or engage with personalities like Wolfman Jack, seeing them as "operating in a bygone era." He vowed to make music "my own way or not at all," prioritizing his artistic integrity over "stupid flashing lights" or contrived appearances. "I get people saying to me all the time Billy you could be a giant a real superstar if you'd only play the game hype yourself be a little more commercial don't be so cynical like everyone really got upset when I told the people from the midnight special. That I wouldn't think of hosting a show like theirs are sitting down and talking to a jerk like Wolfman Jack."
facts.episode: Ep. 51 - The Softer Side of 70s Rock
facts.name: Billy Joel

facts.title: Mid-1975 Evolution
facts.body: In mid-1975, Genesis began a significant evolution influenced by numerous factors beyond just Peter Gabriel's departure. The music market itself was shifting, and despite progressive rock's popularity (with bands like King Crimson and Pink Floyd filling stadiums), Genesis chose to evolve with these market changes and public taste. "a mitad de 1975, justo a mitad de los 70, se dan muchos factores que hacen que el genesis empieza a dar un cambio a dar una evolución."
facts.episode: GENESIS con Peter Gabriel VS. Phil Collins
facts.name: Genesis

facts.title: Punk Fashion Inspiration (1975)
facts.body: During a 1975 trip to New York for a fashion fair, Malcolm McLaren took a detour to CBGBs, where he encountered Richard Hell, then bassist for The Heartbreakers. Hell, due to his poverty, wore ripped clothes held together with safety pins, a look McLaren misinterpreted as a "grand fashion statement," inspiring him to integrate safety pins into his own clothing designs back in England. "What drew Malcolm to Richard was a sense of style or what Malcolm thought to be Richard's sense of style because, well, you see, Richard was actually so poor that he'd wears clothing until they literally fell apart."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 5
facts.name: Malcolm McLaren

facts.title: Encounter with Johnny Rotten (1975)
facts.body: In 1975, Malcolm McLaren's clothing shop served as a significant location in music history. It was here that he encountered Johnny Rotten, who was wearing an "I Hate Pink Floyd" t-shirt, leading to Rotten's consideration for the lead singer role in the Sex Pistols. "Johnny Rotten walked into Malcolm McLaren's clothing shop in 1975. He was immediately considered for the job of lead singer of the sex pistols, based on the fact that he was wearing an eye-hate pink Floyd t-shirt."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 15
facts.name: Malcolm McLaren

facts.title: Dramatic Appearance During "Wish You Were Here" Recordings (1975)
facts.body: In 1975, while Pin Floyd was in the studio completing "Wish You Were Here," Sid Baret unexpectedly appeared, completely shaven, pale, without eyelashes or eyebrows, and in a "horrible state." This moment, captured in two or three historical photos, deeply impacted Roger Waters, who broke down crying upon seeing his childhood friend. This event profoundly changed the lives of the band members and the band's history. "Aparece completamente rapado, muy pálido, sin pestañas, sin cejas, en un estado horrible y según nos cuenta un ayudante ingeniero de sonido que estaba allí, Roger Waters rompía llorar totalmente desgarrado por el estado en el que estaba Sid Baret."
facts.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett
facts.name: Syd Barrett

facts.title: Critical Commentary (Ken Barnes, 1975)
facts.body: In 1975, Ken Barnes wrote that April Wine was overlooked by radio programmers, being considered "too hard for AM" but "not weighty enough for FM progressives." Reviewers scorned them for lacking a "convenient handle" like Bruce Springsteen's "street poetics," 10cc's "verbal manipulations," or The Rolling Stones' "historical legacy," causing record companies to neglect their promotion. "Reviewers scorn them because they don't have the convenient handle."

facts.name: April Wine

facts.title: Grammy Award for Country Performance (1975)
facts.body: The Pointer Sisters won a Grammy Award for Best Country Performance by a Group or Duo in 1975 for their song "Fairy Tale." They held the distinction of being the only African American women to win a country Grammy for 50 years until Beyoncé's win in 2024. "Fairy tale earned the pointer sisters a Grammy Award... for best country performance by a group or duo in 1975."

facts.title: Flagship Songwriter - 1975 Breakthrough LP
facts.body: For Fleetwood Mac's 1975 self-titled breakthrough album, Christine McVie once again proved to be the band's flagship songwriter, with her songs chosen as the lead singles on both sides of the Atlantic. "Warm Ways" was the lead single in England, and "Over My Head" in America, the latter becoming their first American Top 40 hit. "Again, she was still the band's flagship songwriter."

facts.title: Two of Three Singles on Breakthrough LP - 1975
facts.body: Christine McVie wrote two out of the three singles released from Fleetwood Mac's 1975 self-titled breakthrough LP, "Over My Head" and "Say You Love Me." These songs were crucial in the album's success, which eventually reached number one on the Billboard album chart and set a record for the longest climb to the top. "Yep, two out of the three singles on Fleetwood Mack's breakthrough LP were by McVease."

facts.title: Formation and Inspiration (1975)
facts.body: The Runaways were formed by producer Kim Fowley, who was inspired by the success of the all-female band Fanny. Active from 1975 to 1979, they are arguably recognized as the first all-female hard rock band, featuring future stars Joan Jett and Lita Ford. "The first is to a weirdo producer named Kim Fowley, who was inspired by the group to form the Runaways, arguably the first all-female hard rock band."

facts.title: Cleveland Origin and Sound (1975)
facts.body: Pere Ubu emerged from Cleveland, having reorganized from the band Rocket from the Tombs in 1975. They were part of a scene of "extreme groups" that were artsy, anti-hippie, anti-establishment, and experimental. They began releasing self-produced indie singles in 1975. "Eventually we organized itself as Pair Ubu. In 1975, they began to release a series of self-produced indie singles that reached a few selecteers around North America. And even as far away as the UK."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Double Album of Pure Guitar Feedback Delivered as Contract FU
facts.body: Unhappy with RCA Records and contractually obligated to deliver one more album, Lou Reed recorded a double album of nothing but guitar feedback in his New York apartment: two guitars given weird tunings, placed in front of amplifiers and left to feed back on themselves for 64 minutes, recorded on a small 4-track machine. Side four of the vinyl featured a locked groove that played infinitely. RCA retaliated by actually releasing it, hoping to destroy his career — and it did, sending his career into a decade-long decline. The record was later reissued on CD in 2000, re-evaluated as an important milestone in industrial, ambient, drone, and doom music. A German ensemble called Zeichkratzer performed and recorded it live around the turn of the millennium, arranged for strings, wind instruments, piano, and accordion. "What began as a really dumb career move turned into revered art."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: 10 Terrible Career Moves
facts.name: Metal Machine Music

facts.title: 64 Minutes of Guitar Feedback as Contract Retaliation; Later Reissued and Covered
facts.body: Lou Reed was contractually obligated to deliver one more album to RCA and wanted out. He set up guitars with unusual tunings in front of amplifiers in his New York City apartment, let them feed back on themselves, and recorded everything on a small 4-track. The resulting double album ran 64 minutes; side four of the vinyl ended in a locked groove that played forever. RCA released it as a counterattack hoping to end his career — it worked for nearly a decade. However, the record was later re-evaluated as an important forerunner of industrial, ambient, drone, and doom music. It has been reissued on CD (2000, Buddha Records) and has sold more than 100,000 copies total. A 10-person German ensemble called Zeichkratzer began performing it live around 2000 and released their own recording of it in 2014, arranged for strings, wind instruments, piano, and accordion. Sonic Youth used samples from it in their own work. "Since its release in 1975, Metal Machine Music has sold more than 100,000 copies."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: 100 Weirdest Things in Alt-Rock: Part 1
facts.name: Metal Machine Music

facts.body: Released in 1975 as a "big FU" to RCA Records, with whom Reed was in a contract dispute, the double album features 64 minutes of abrasive noise across four sides. The final groove on side four was closed, causing the needle to loop endlessly, creating continuous noise. Despite its un-listenability, some consider it a landmark in avant-garde music. "So as a big FU, he released a double album called Metal Machine Music."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 3: Industrial
facts.name: Metal Machine Music

facts.body: Released in the summer of 1975, this double album was created by Lou Reed as a deliberate act of defiance against RCA, from whom he wanted to exit his contract. Contractually obligated to deliver more albums, Reed produced "Metal Machine Music," a work consisting of over four sides of continuous noise and feedback. Reed claimed to be channeling avant-garde composers like La Monte Young and Iannis Xenakis, and even Beethoven, though the album is primarily recognized for its weaponized, sustained distortion and locked groove on side four, designed to play infinitely. RCA released it as an "in-your-face" move back at Lou, and its sounds even inspired the Breene language in "Star Trek: The Next Generation." "Lou recorded a double album. Now to hear Lou explain what he did, he was merely channeling the experimental spirit of an avant-garde composer from the 1960s named Le Mans Young."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Distortion and Feedback
facts.name: Metal Machine Music

facts.title: First Show October 17, 1975 – Pre-dates Sex Pistols and The Clash; 1980 Ontario Place Riot
facts.body: Teenage Head formed in Hamilton, Ontario, and played their first show on October 17, 1975 at Westdale High School — three weeks before the Sex Pistols played their first gig, and nine months before The Clash formed. They were a major force in Canadian punk, combining elements of the Ramones, New York Dolls, and 1950s rock and roll. Their profile peaked with a 1980 show at Ontario Place in Toronto where thousands tried to get in; what followed became an infamous riot. American radio programmers loved the music but balked at the band name (for obvious reasons), prompting a temporary rename to "Teenage Heads" for US purposes. Just before a crucial US showcase in September 1980, guitarist Gord Lewis was in a serious car accident, canceling the shows and closing the window of opportunity. Original singer Frankie Venom died of throat cancer in 2008; the band continues with Dave Rave on vocals more than 40 years later. "Long after most of their original punk rock contemporaries called it quits, or died off, Teenage Head still with us."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: 14 Important Canadian Punk Bands
facts.name: Teenage Head

facts.title: Unwitting Punk Fashion Catalyst (1975)
facts.body: In 1975, while serving as the bassist for The Heartbreakers, Richard Hell met Malcolm McLaren at CBGBs in New York. Due to his impoverished circumstances, Hell wore his clothing until it literally fell apart, then used safety pins to hold the ripped scraps together. McLaren, misinterpreting this as a deliberate "grand fashion statement," adopted the idea and brought it back to England, where it became a cornerstone of nascent punk fashion. "What drew Malcolm to Richard was a sense of style or what Malcolm thought to be Richard's sense of style because, well, you see, Richard was actually so poor that he'd wears clothing until they literally fell apart. And once they did that, he'd hold the rip scraps of cloth together with safety pins."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 5
facts.name: Richard "Hell"

facts.body: Patti Smith's commercial breakthrough album, released in 1975, was described as "poetry that was set on fire" and an "invocation." Produced by John Cale of The Velvet Underground, the record was characterized by a chaotic yet spiritual essence, with chaos being "kind of the point." It opened with a rewritten version of Van Morrison's "Gloria," featuring the line "Jesus died for somebody's sins but not mine," setting a tone of independence and transforming punk into art. "Horses wasn't really just music, it was kind of like this invocation. It opened with her rewriting Van Morrison's Gloria and she kind of turned it into this declaration of her own independence."
facts.episode: Ep. 57 - Punk and New Wave at New York's CBGB
facts.name: Horses

facts.body: Patti Smith's debut album, "Horses," blended the spirituality of the Beat generation with a raw, punk sensibility, even though the term "punk" was not yet widely applied to music. This album was a vehicle for Smith to recite, scream, and challenge the traditional role of women in music. "Su primer disco, Jorge, mezclaba la espiritualidad beat con una clúdeza punk, aunque aún no se le llamara así."
facts.episode: El punk existía antes de Sex Pistols (y era algo salvaje)
facts.name: Horses

facts.body: Released at the end of November 1975, this debut album was an "epiphany moment" for outsiders and those seeking alternative forms of rock and pop. Michael Stipe of REM described buying it on release day, listening all night, and being a "changed person," calling it one of the defining moments in his life. "When Patty Smith's record came out of the end of November 1975, it was another one of those epiphany moments for weirdos, outsiders, and those who were actively searching for alternative forms of rock and pop."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 4
facts.name: Horses

facts.body: Released in November 1975, this was Patti Smith's first and most important record. Its release coincided with the Sex Pistols' first gig and predated the Ramones' debut album by six months, making it a powerful and influential work for many female punks and future Riot Girls. "Patty's most important record was probably her first one, Horses, November 1975."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Riot Grrrls - A Primer

facts.title: Commercial Breakthrough
facts.body: Patti Smith's commercial breakthrough album, released in 1975, was described as "poetry that was set on fire" and an "invocation." Produced by John Cale of The Velvet Underground, the record was characterized by a chaotic yet spiritual essence, with chaos being "kind of the point." It opened with a rewritten version of Van Morrison's "Gloria," featuring the line "Jesus died for somebody's sins but not mine," setting a tone of independence and transforming punk into art. "Horses wasn't really just music, it was kind of like this invocation. It opened with her rewriting Van Morrison's Gloria and she kind of turned it into this declaration of her own independence."

facts.name: Horses

facts.title: Record Label Pressure and Refusal to Move (1975)
facts.body: After "Jackie Blue" fell from the charts, their label, A&M, pressured them to produce more "Jackie" themed hits (e.g., "Jackie Red," "Jackie Green," "Jackie Brown"). The band refused, stating they did not approach their music that way. A&M then tried to persuade them to move to Los Angeles for increased TV exposure, but the band, many of whom were starting families and had farms in Missouri, collectively decided to stay, prioritizing their lifestyle over potential massive fame. "We all decided to stay in Missouri."

facts.title: Refused by Billy Joel (1975)
facts.body: In 1975, a 26-year-old Billy Joel refused to engage with commercial media figures, including "sitting down and talking to a jerk like Wolfman Jack" for shows like *Midnight Special*, viewing them as representatives of "a bygone era." "everyone really got upset when I told the people from the midnight special. That I wouldn't think of hosting a show like theirs are sitting down and talking to a jerk like Wolfman Jack."

facts.title: 1975 CMA Awards Incident - Card Burning
facts.body: As the reigning CMA entertainer of the year, Charlie Rich staggered onto the stage at Nashville's Grand Ole Opry in 1975, fueled by gin and tonics, and announced John Denver as the winner. He then pulled out a lighter and set the card with Denver's name on it on fire, an act widely interpreted as a statement that John Denver was not welcome in country music. Rich later claimed it was an accident caused by pain killers. "Rich reaches into his pocket, takes out a lighter and sets the card with Denver's name on it on fire."
facts.episode: Ep. 2 - Countryish Music of the 1970s (Encore)
facts.name: Charlie Rich

facts.title: 1975 CMA Award Presentation Incident
facts.body: During the 1975 CMAs, Charlie Rich was scheduled to present the New Entertainer of the Year award. Upon opening the envelope and seeing John Denver's name, Rich controversially used a lighter to set the slip of paper on fire before announcing Denver as the winner. This bizarre act was later attributed to Rich being intoxicated and under the influence of pain medication, with him reportedly believing it was humorous. However, to the CMA audience, it was widely perceived as a protest against the increasing "popification" of country music, a sentiment that had been recently fueled by debates involving Olivia Newton-John. "rich, open the envelope, and when he saw John Denver's name there, took out a lighter and lit the slip of paper on fire."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

facts.title: Crowned Queen of Disco Texts (1975)
facts.body: In February 1975, Gloria Gaynor was officially crowned the "Queen of Disco Texts" by the newly formed National Association of Disco Tech Disc Jockeys at a disco in New York. She was presented with a crown, a 30-pound velvet cape, and a trophy, expressing her delight at the acknowledgment. "Gainer was literally crowned the Queen of Disco Texts in February 1975 by the newly created National Association of Disco Tech disc jockeys."
facts.episode: Ep. 1 - Disco Doesn't Suck (Encore)
facts.name: Gloria Gaynor

facts.title: Discomfort with Commercial Success (1975)
facts.body: Following the hit "Miracles" and the commercial success of *Red Octopus*, she expressed discomfort, stating, "when miracles hit it was all of a sudden better stick with that shit but I felt odd doing it like I was wearing a costume a monkey suit or something." This highlights her internal struggle with the band's shift from counterculture to pop. "Grace licks said when miracles hit it was all of a sudden better stick with that shit but I felt odd doing it like I was wearing a costume a monkey suit or something."
facts.episode: Ep. 51 - The Softer Side of 70s Rock
facts.name: Grace Slick
